components.note: Finite nonempty outcome set, power-set events, mass function, induced measure, complement, disjointness, support, null and almost-sure events; boundary remarks on the source term "distribution function" (Grinstead-Snell Definition 1.2) and on the uniformity assumption behind counting.
Empty/whole, bounds, monotonicity, finite additivity incl. m=0, complement and union formulas, null-event criterion, converse atomic representation with uniqueness; full proof.
Finite-valued random variables, events {X in D}, law, joint variable and law, marginals, composition; boundary on zero-mass values.
Laws are mass functions, P(X in D), both marginalization identities, law of f(X); proof by fibers incl. empty fibers.
P(A|B) for P(B)>0, conditional measure and mass function, interpretation boundary.
p_B is a mass function, P(B|B)=1, multiplication rule, chain rule with positive-prefix hypothesis, successive conditioning; proof incl. null final intersection.
Explicit null conditioning event with 0/0, non-determination by multiplication, almost-sure event omitting outcomes.
Partition, prior weights, J, likelihoods, posterior weights, odds; likelihoods need not sum to one.
Total probability with J, Bayes formula with null-prior branch, posteriors sum to one, odds form with q0>0; proof.
Two-event, mutual and pairwise independence, finite-valued random-variable independence, conditional independence given H.
Conditional criterion, null events, complements, event-form equivalence for random variables, product construction; proof.
Explicit four-point model: pairwise but not mutually independent; conditioning on C destroys independence of A,B (arithmetic checked).
Stipulated defect/alert model with numbers, base-rate variant 2/3, two-alert conditionally independent model 36/47, copied-alert boundary 2/13 (arithmetic checked).
Real-valued variable, expectation, indicator, pointwise arithmetic, {X=Y}, composition.
Grouping formula E[f(X)], E[1_A]=P(A), linearity without independence, monotonicity, independent product; proof.
Indicator count, linearity under dependence, failure of product factorization for 1_A*1_A.
E[X|B] for P(B)>0 and E[X|Y] with declared zero on null fibers and a.s. irrelevance of that choice.
Partition averaging with J, averaging property over Y-events, tower identity, a.s. uniqueness among h(Y); proof; worked alert example at lines 440-451.
Scope warning: model justification, no estimation/causal/prior selection, LLN needed for empirical interpretation, excluded general theory.

Mutual/pairwise independence of events, collections and sub-sigma-algebras over finite or countable index sets, empty-intersection convention, finite-subfamily definition for infinite families, and the boundary that it does not construct an infinite product measure.

Independence of random elements in general measurable spaces, Borel value sigma-algebra for real variables, sigma(X_i), pairwise variant, identically distributed and i.i.d. definitions, with the boundary that equal laws do not imply independence.

Durrett 2.1.1-2.1.3 generalized: sigma(X_i) equivalence, complements (single, successive, countable), indicator and sigma({A_i}) equivalence, self-independence iff probability 0/1, conditional-probability form, a.s. replacement without completion; full annex proof.
Lemma 2.1.5 (adjoining Omega) and Theorem 2.1.7 with written lambda-system verification, pi-lambda step, coordinate-by-coordinate iteration and countable extension.
Theorem 2.1.8 with t_i in R or infinity, rational-threshold sufficiency, countable-family form; proof via pi-system of threshold events and generator theorem.
Theorems 2.1.9-2.1.10 for countable disjoint groups, empty group, f_i(X_i), finite real blocks, measurability caveat for countable groups; proof including direct Exercise 2.1.6 argument.
Source application S_n-S_m independent of 1{max_{k<=m} S_k > a}, with measurability of both block functions and disjoint-block justification.
Theorem 2.1.11 (both directions), finite construction from prescribed laws and distribution functions (source p.53), countable-valued criterion (Exercise 2.1.2), with proofs.
Theorems 2.1.12-2.1.13 nonnegative and integrable cases, n-fold product with induction and 0*infinity convention, and bounded-function converse characterization, with proofs.
Covariance, uncorrelatedness, correlation (undefined for zero variance), uncorrelated family; existence verified in the annex.
Cov formula, Cauchy-Schwarz bound, independence implies zero covariance, weighted finite-sum variance formula (generalizing Theorem 2.2.1) with only pairwise conditions needed; proof written.

Four explicit countermodels: Example 2.1.4 with its model, Exercise 2.1.9 generator counterexample, Example 2.1.14 with full parameter range, and self-independence failure of a fair bit; computations written in annex (arithmetic checked).

Method entry for establishing independence (thresholds, joint law, point masses, disjoint groups, absolute moments) with the boundary that pairwise or zero-covariance checks do not give full factorization.
Exercise 2.1.15 dyadic bits on the constructed unit interval: floor formula, parity agreement, measurability, finite-pattern probability 2^{-#J}, mutual independence; full annex proof.
Lemma 2.2.2 and Theorem 2.2.3 (L2 weak law with explicit C/n and Chebyshev bounds) plus worked application to fair bits; full annex proof.
